original_question: How can one characterize the possible shapes of bounded or unbounded non-convex expectation-parameter spaces that arise from non-steep exponential families?
target_in_paper: Section 7 (Tomonari Sei): "How to characterize possible shapes of non-convex expectation parameter spaces?" ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target: it focuses on characterizing non-convex expectation-parameter spaces and correctly brings in the paper’s contextual point that such phenomena occur only in the non-steep setting. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
missing_details: The paper makes the notation explicit: the expectation-parameter space is M = ∇ψ(Θ), so a stand-alone question should define ψ, Θ, and M rather than referring only informally to an "expectation-parameter space." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The relevant condition is steepness of the potential function ψ, defined here by the statement that the gradient map diverges at every boundary point of Θ; this should be stated explicitly. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The paper uses a one-way implication, not an equivalence: if ψ is steep, then M is the interior of the convex closure of supp(ν), hence non-convex M can appear only if ψ is non-steep. Your draft should not suggest that non-steepness alone is the whole characterization. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

A paper-faithful version should include the further necessary condition recorded in Section 7: when M is non-convex, the support of the underlying measure ν must be unbounded. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The emphasis on "bounded or unbounded" is not the paper’s official formulation. In the paper, boundedness is contextual: after noting the unbounded-support necessity, the authors give an example showing that M itself may nevertheless be bounded and non-convex. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or "for all sufficiently large m" clause is part of this problem. The missing data are instead the statistical-geometric definitions above. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
refined_question: Let ν be a measure on ℝ^d, let ψ(θ) = log ∫ e^{⟨θ,x⟩} ν(dx), let Θ = {θ ∈ ℝ^d : ψ(θ) < ∞}, and let M := ∇ψ(Θ) be the expectation-parameter space of the associated exponential family. Since the paper notes that if ψ is steep then M is the interior of conv(supp ν), so any non-convex M can occur only in the non-steep case and necessarily requires unbounded supp(ν), while Figure 1 shows that M can still be bounded and non-convex, characterize the subsets M ⊂ ℝ^d that can arise as non-convex expectation-parameter spaces of such exponential families. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper because Section 7 first recalls Efron’s non-convex example, then gives the steep/non-steep context and the definition M = ∇ψ(Θ), and finally states the open question verbatim as a shape-classification problem. The draft is close but slightly less faithful because it foregrounds the bounded/unbounded dichotomy, whereas the paper’s actual target is the overall characterization of possible non-convex shapes, with boundedness appearing only as an illustrative example. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
